clue.text: What's good in dish topped with pastry covering?

definitions.text: What's good in dish topped with pastry covering?

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside that other thing

blocks.note: a pie is a dish with a pastry top
G is the standard abbreviation for good
something on another thing is covering it

explanation.surface: A question about what makes a tasty filling under a pie crust.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also defines the answer, since pigeon pie is a classic British dish with the bird under a pastry lid.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigeon is a traditional pie filling, so the bird is literally the good stuff under the pastry lid.

clue.text: It's addressed by message — other side often has a view

definitions.text: It's addressed by message — other side often has a view

blocks.note: surface reading: something being dealt with by sending a message

blocks.clueFragment: other side often has a view
blocks.note: setter's reading: a card with an address and a message on one side and a picture of scenery on the back

explanation.walkthrough: 'Addressed' suggests tackling a problem, but it means literally bearing an address next to a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday card carries the address and a short note on the back, with a scenic photograph on the front.

clue.text: Non-specific info on Central American?

indicators.note: central means only the middle of the following word is wanted

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
the middle four letters of the eight-letter word

explanation.surface: A question about vague information on someone from Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central American' looks like a region's people, but 'Central' picks the middle letters of American.
explanation.definitionFit: Generic describes something general, applying to a whole class rather than one particular item.

clue.text: Line I inserted in manifest that's not sensible

indicators.note: things inserted in something else are placed inside it

blocks.note: manifest means plain to see
L is the abbreviation for line
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that a line added to a ship's manifest makes no sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sensible' here has its older meaning of aware or conscious of something, not reasonable.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone oblivious is unaware, and sensible in the old sense means aware, so not sensible fits.

clue.text: Like every story and old record

blocks.note: first meaning: as the saying goes, there are two sides to every story
second meaning: a vinyl single with an A-side and a B-side

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning leans on the proverb 'there are two sides to every story'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a pair of faces or viewpoints describes both a disputed account and a vinyl disc.

clue.text: Endlessly wine and dine people in bar? Blow that!

indicators.note: without an end means the last letter of each word is dropped
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: wine without its last letter
dine without its last letter
a strut is a supporting bar in a frame
men as a general word for people

explanation.surface: Someone declining to treat staff in a pub to food and drink: 'Blow that!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, but here it is a rigid rod; 'Blow that!' sounds like a refusal, yet it describes the answer as a thing to blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpet or flute is played by breath, so a wind instrument is a thing you blow.

clue.text: Barely finished performance in sporting outfit

blocks.note: first meaning: a striptease act, which ends with the performer bare
second meaning: the kit a team wears

explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely' looks like 'only just', but it means ending up bare. A team's strip is its kit in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an undressing act on stage and the shirts and shorts a football side wears.

clue.text: Stray fruit I have cut up inside

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
inside means placed within the other word

blocks.note: a date is a fruit of the palm
contraction I've

explanation.surface: Someone wandering off after slicing up some fruit indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' refers to the contraction losing letters, and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To deviate is to wander off course, the same verb as stray.

clue.text: Present put on a tree, oddly

indicators.note: oddly asks for only the letters in odd positions of the word

blocks.note: to don clothes is to put them on
taken as written
first and third letters

explanation.surface: A gift placed under the Christmas tree in a strange way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To present something formally is to give it, and donate is a synonym for giving.

clue.text: Rebranded a star, transformed into leader of movement

indicators.note: something transformed is changed into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A celebrity is given a makeover and becomes the face of a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard-bearer carried a flag at the head of troops; figuratively it is the prominent champion of a cause.

clue.text: Short suit or vest being worn

blocks.note: a singlet is a sleeveless vest
clothes being worn are on

explanation.surface: A choice between a short suit or a vest for wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short suit' looks like clothing, matching vest, but it is a bridge term.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a singleton is a holding of only one card in a suit, the shortest possible suit.

clue.text: Headless chicken or other bird

indicators.note: without a head means the first letter is removed

blocks.note: chicken as an adjective means cowardly

explanation.surface: A choice between a frantic headless chicken and some different bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' wants to be the bird, but it means cowardly; 'other bird' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The raven is a large black corvid, a bird other than the chicken already mentioned.

clue.text: One vehicle after another for group of travellers

indicators.note: after places the first pieces behind the closing one

blocks.note: a car is another vehicle
a means one
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A line of vehicles, nose to tail, carrying a party of travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' stands for another vehicle, so a car comes first, followed by one van.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravan is a company of travellers journeying together, as with merchants crossing a desert.

clue.text: Insert minute sketch in it

indicators.note: in means placed inside the word that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for minute
a plan is a sketch or outline

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a tiny drawing inside something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' reads as tiny, but it is the unit of time, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: To implant is to set something firmly into place, a synonym of the verb insert.

clue.text: Member of clergy clipped page three, for example

indicators.note: something clipped has its end trimmed off

blocks.note: a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A cleric pictured on a tabloid's page three, hinting at scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Page three suggests the Sun newspaper's notorious page, but here it is simply an odd-numbered page.
explanation.definitionFit: The recto is the right-hand page of an open book, always odd-numbered, so page three is one.

clue.text: Took in gold found in berth?

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside the following phrase

blocks.note: a berth is a sailor's bed, and AB is an able seaman
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A question whether someone took in gold that was discovered in a ship's bunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading of berth as AB'S BED, an able seaman's bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb is to soak up or take in, so the past tense matches took in.

clue.text: Think about past crimes in reformed state, ultimately

indicators.note: reformed means formed again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
ultimately points to the very last letter of the word

blocks.note: taken as written
final letter

explanation.surface: A reformed criminal looks back on past offences.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to recall and talk about earlier experiences, thinking about the past.

clue.text: Went hunting, as happened before

blocks.note: first meaning: acted as a predator
second meaning: came earlier in time

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense comes from predator; the second is pre plus dated.
explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling serves as the past tense of preying as a predator and of occurring earlier than something.

clue.text: Reverse as taken to heart by less polished campaigner

indicators.note: reverse tells us to read the little word backwards
taken to heart means placed in the middle of the other word

blocks.note: cruder means rougher
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rough-edged activist who takes a setback to heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' looks like a noun meaning a setback, but it is the instruction for the little word that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusader is someone who campaigns vigorously for a cause.

clue.text: Drink everything contained by overturned canisters

indicators.note: all the letters sit inside the following word
turned over in a down clue means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the word without its outer letters

explanation.surface: A drink that is all poured out of upturned tins.
explanation.walkthrough: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a resinated Greek wine, so it is an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Half-hearted American playwright's competitor, in long run

indicators.note: half of the heart goes, so one of the doubled central letters is dropped

blocks.note: Arthur Miller wrote Death of a Salesman

explanation.surface: A lukewarm American dramatist seen as a rival over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the long run' sounds like 'eventually', but here it is a race of a mile.
explanation.definitionFit: A miler is an athlete who specialises in races over one mile, a long run.

clue.text: Pound is small, housing single feline

indicators.note: housing means holding something inside

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling
taken as written
single means one
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: An animal pound is small, keeping just one cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' suggests an enclosure for animals, but it is money, the pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: A lioness is a female lion, one of the big cats, so she is a feline.

clue.text: Prince again securing academic title

indicators.note: securing means holding something firmly within

blocks.note: anew means once more
Dr, doctor, is an academic title

explanation.surface: A prince once more earning a university degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Andrew is the brother of King Charles III, so the name is an example of a prince.

clue.text: Significant reason for not eating in restaurant

definitions.text: reason for not eating in restaurant

blocks.note: first meaning: important

blocks.clueFragment: reason for not eating in restaurant
blocks.note: second meaning: read as two words, there was nowhere free to sit

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer after the second letter to get the restaurant excuse: no table.
explanation.definitionFit: Something notable is worthy of attention, so it is important or significant.

clue.text: Triumphant cry from British dominating home game

indicators.note: in a down clue, dominating means sitting above the rest

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
at home means in
go is a turn in a game, and also the board game

explanation.surface: A cheer from a British team that has the upper hand in a home match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home game' looks like a fixture at one's own ground; the two words split into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo is the shout of the winner in the numbers game, used generally as an exclamation of success.

clue.text: Male with an indication of scholarly achievement, not youth

blocks.note: a man is a male
a graduate's academic hood shows the degree held

explanation.surface: A man in graduation dress, no longer a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: Manhood is the state of being an adult man, the stage after youth has ended.

clue.text: E.g. alternating with king or queen in monarchy

indicators.note: alternating means the two sets of letters take turns, one from each

blocks.note: R stands for rex or regina, king or queen
first letter of the abbreviation, taken in turn
first letter of the little word, taken in turn
second letter of the abbreviation, taken in turn
second letter of the little word, taken in turn

explanation.surface: Kings and queens taking turns on the throne, as happens in a monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: After the regal R, the letters of 'E.g.' and 'in' take turns, one from each, rather than following each other as whole words.
explanation.definitionFit: A reign is the rule of a sovereign, the period of monarchical government.

clue.text: Different entrances needed on the way back up

indicators.note: different signals that the word is made into something else by reordering

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Extra doorways required on a route returning uphill.
explanation.definitionFit: Renascent means being reborn or reviving, recovering after a decline.

clue.text: Tired holding power supported by arms

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside

blocks.note: weary means tired
P is the symbol for power
a thing on another is held up by it

explanation.surface: An exhausted regime holding on to power thanks to its military.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms' could suggest limbs holding things up, but it means weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms are weapons collectively, which is exactly what weaponry denotes.

clue.text: Reached finish with no difficulty, breaking record

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

blocks.note: a CD is a compact disc, a record
ease is freedom from difficulty

explanation.surface: An athlete crossed the line comfortably, setting a new record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking record' sounds like setting a new best, but here it means going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease is to stop or come to an end, so ceased means reached its finish.
